why: A search reports `examined`, the rows its calls checked - the candidates their engine supplied, every one checked by the library - and `searched_on`, one entry per combination of fields the calls looked in, sorted, with the number of calls, in code point order. Two calls that named the same fields in another order are one entry, and a failed call counts what it examined before it failed. A search takes no filter, so it has no `filtered_on`, and it filtered on no time: time_filtered_share is a measured 0. The text the searches looked for is in no document.
